findings.title: Querying `get_memory_info()` per process buffer double-counts Redis cluster memory and repeats `INFO` calls
findings.body: In `SpanFlusher.submit`, the code now iterates over `self.buffers.values()` and extends `memory_infos` with `buffer.get_memory_info()` from each `SpansBuffer` instance. Because `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()` queries memory across all hosts in the Redis cluster (`self.client.hosts`), calling it once per flusher process repeats the same Redis `INFO` network calls `num_processes` times on every `submit()` and duplicates the `ServiceMemory` entries in `memory_infos`. While `used / available` remains mathematically identical if all hosts are weighted equally, it causes `N` times as many Redis `INFO` calls on the main consumer thread. `get_memory_info()` only needs to be called on a single buffer instance (or the parent `buffer`).

findings.title: `join()` leaves remaining flusher processes running if the timeout expires on an earlier process
findings.body: In `SpanFlusher.join()`, the loop over `self.processes.items()` checks `if remaining_time <= 0: break` before reaching `process.terminate()`. If the first process takes the full timeout (or `next_step.join(timeout)` already consumed it), the loop breaks early and never calls `process.terminate()` on the remaining processes in `self.processes`, leaving orphan background flusher processes running after consumer shutdown/rebalance. Instead of breaking out of the loop, it should skip the `while process.is_alive()` wait and still terminate every remaining `multiprocessing.Process`.

findings.title: Inconsistent metric tag name `shards` vs `shard` on `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce`
findings.body: Lines 185 and 195 tag `spans.buffer.flusher.produce` and `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes` with `tags={"shard": shard_tag}`, whereas line 199 tags `spans.buffer.flusher.wait_produce` with `tags={"shards": shard_tag}` (plural). This makes the tag key inconsistent across the flusher metrics.
